Photograph: Wason Wanichakorn/AP Thailand Thailand school shooting toll rises to nine after 12-year-old dies, police say Teenage girl treated in hospital after Friday’s school shooting has died, police say Staff and agencies Sat 8 Aug 2026 22.11 EDT Last modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 02.24 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The death toll from a school shooting in Thailand rose to nine on Saturday, after police said a 12-year-old girl caught up in Friday’s incident had died. Police at the Plai Bang Police Station in Nonthaburi Province said the girl, who had been treated at hospital with critical wounds, had died, a day after a 14-year-old boy allegedly shot his grandparents and then killed more people at his school before turning the gun on ⁠himself. Thailand school shooting: eight killed including suspected attacker, police say Read more The 14-year-old wounded more than 30 people in the ⁠shooting at the Debsirin Nonthaburi school northwest of Bangkok. Fourteen people remained in hospital on Saturday evening, seven of them in critical condition. Police are questioning more witnesses as part of their investigation, including the suspect’s parents. The boy had lived with his grandparents for 12 years after his parents had separated, Atthapol Anusit, deputy commissioner of the Provincial Police Region 1, ‌told reporters on Sunday. The suspected attacker fired at least 26 bullets with a gun belonging to his grandfather, and was found with 34 additional ammunition rounds. Police on Sunday told reporters the teenager had an air ⁠gun confiscated by a teacher last year and had watched violent content online and used social media to learn how to ⁠use a firearm. “According to witness interviews, the perpetrator had begun showing interest in ​studying the use of firearms ‌for some time, about one ‌to two years,” Atthapol said. Atthapol, who said police had so far interviewed 17 witnesses, said a knife had also been found in the boy’s bag and other evidence found at the crime scenes included a firearm, spent cartridge cases, and a personal computer. On the day of the incident, the suspected shooter remained inside the school after reports of the attack emerged, Arsit Sampantharat, the permanent secretary of the interior ministry, told PPTV. A lockdown at the school was declared over in about half an hour. Images from the scene showed students running with only socks on their feet as they were evacuated from the school. Thailand’s prime minister, Anutin Charnvirakul, has vowed to implement new gun laws, telling reporters only government officials on duty would be allowed to carry guns. However, he did not provide any ⁠specifics, including whether the legislation would tighten gun ownership requirements. Thailand has the highest rate of civilian gun ownership in south-east Asia, and in 2017 the Switzerland-based Small Arms Survey placed the country 13th worldwide for small-gun possession. A number of mass shootings have occurred in recent years in Thailand, including incidents at schools and a large Bangkok mall, and a 2022 attack in the country’s north-east that ‌killed 37 people including 22 children. https://www.mediafax.ro/english/the-magi.text: „The Magic of AUR”: Buzoianu claims that the AUR party „votes for nothing in the judiciary to change” In a post uploaded to Facebook on Friday, Diana Buzoianu wrote about „the magic of AUR, which lies that it is anti-system and then votes so that nothing in the judiciary changes.” According to the minister, at the moment „in the legal committee in Parliament, justice reform projects with the votes of AUR and PSD are being put on the conveyor belt.” What reforms will not be voted on by the PSD? Diana Buzoianu specifies that PSD will vote against reforms initiated by USR. „PSD has put on the agenda the justice reform package initiated by USR and is voting against it. They will vote, for example, against the USR project that demands that the secondments and delegations of judges be made much more objectively so that after years of trials from scratch are not resumed. As was the case with the gift recently given to Negoiță by the Bucharest Court of Appeal,” she wrote. On the other hand, the interim Minister of the Environment says that AUR will abstain from the vote. „AUR is opposing. They will abstain from voting on everything. They have already done this on the first projects in the package. It’s just that they don’t know exactly what they should vote for, the poor AUR people, for example, on a bill that requires judges to no longer be seconded/delegated without clear explanations, thus resuming from 0 trials that have been pending for years with damages of billions or corruption crimes at the highest level,” she continues. However, Buzoianu states that AUR is based on the fact that people do not know that the abstention vote is calculated as a vote for the rejection report, not for the approval report. „In committees, the abstention vote is counted as a vote for the rejection report, not for the approval report. It’s just that AUR relies on the fact that people don’t know these details and leave committees convinced that no one saw them kiss the PSD ring and sell out justice (what exactly should they say).” Buzoianu: „AUR and PSD planned to reject projects today” Buzoianu says that AUR does not have the courage to assume its vote. NATO is monitoring recent attacks on commercial vessels in and around the Black Sea, including two in Romanian territorial waters. (Regina Koesters/U.S. Army) By JOHN VANDIVER STARS AND STRIPES Published October 15, 2026 · NATO’s top military commander is consulting with defense chiefs as the bloc monitors a string of attacks on commercial vessels in and around the Black Sea, including two vessels targeted in Romanian territorial waters, alliance officials said Thursday. U.S. Air Force Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, NATO’s supreme allied commander in Europe and head of U.S. European Command, and his deputy are in close contact with allied military leaders over the matter. Consulting one another is “exactly what they need to be doing at this time,” Col. Martin O’Donnell, spokesman for Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, said in a statement to Stars and Stripes. The incidents are the latest suspected drone attacks on commercial shipping near NATO’s southeastern flank, as risks from Russia’s war in Ukraine reach beyond the battlefield. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said Thursday that he had met with Romanian and Bulgarian leaders to discuss Black Sea security and that the alliance has strengthened its military posture in the area. Romanian President Nicusor Dan has called for stronger allied measures to protect Black Sea shipping as the investigation unfolds. “We went to NATO, to our allies, and stated that we need equipment to ensure the protection of a NATO state on the Danube (River),” Dan said Thursday, as quoted by Romanian media. “Now we are having the same discussion regarding the Black Sea.” The latest incidents follow a series of drone attacks against commercial shipping near Bulgaria , including attacks that left some sailors dead or missing. The threat has prompted Bulgaria to announce plans to join a NATO counter-drone initiative by the end of October and purchase additional equipment to protect its territory. According to NATO, four commercial vessels were targeted overnight Wednesday and early Thursday. Two of them, the Marshall Islands-flagged bulk carrier Sea Destiny and the Comoros-flagged tanker Yara J, were targeted in Romanian territorial waters, NATO said. A third vessel, the San Marino-flagged chemical tanker Wine Trader, was targeted just outside Romania’s territorial waters. The fourth, the Tanzanian-flagged tanker Dania J, was targeted in the Danube at the Ukrainian port of Izmail, near the Romanian border. Romanian authorities are investigating the first three incidents, NATO said. The alliance did not identify who was responsible for the attacks or say whether drones struck all four vessels. The incidents coincided with three drone incursions into Romanian airspace near the Ukrainian border that prompted NATO fighter jets to scramble Wednesday and early Thursday. Spanish F-18 Hornets assigned to NATO’s enhanced air policing mission were launched from Mihail Kogalniceanu Air Base during an overnight alert, NATO said. Romanian F-16s also responded. That incident followed two other drone incursions on Wednesday. NATO Europe Drones John Vandiver covers U.S. military activities across Europe and Africa. Based in Stuttgart, Germany, he previously worked for newspapers in New Jersey, North Carolina and Maryland. He is a graduate of the University of Delaware.
